# Pilot — Bloomington, Indiana (Open311)

**Real data.** Generated by `tools/adapters/open311.py` from the live Open311 GeoReport v2
endpoint.

```bash
python3 tools/adapters/open311.py --url https://bloomington.in.gov/crm/open311/v2 \
  --name Bloomington --limit 60 --out examples/pilot-bloomington-311
```

60 service requests, 63 services in the catalogue.

The `requests` profile carries the strongest opinion in schemaGov — that reporter privacy is
a schema concern, enforced by a validator that fails the build on personal data. This is the
test of that opinion against a real 311 feed.

## The opinion was right, and aimed slightly wrong

**The field check passed cleanly.** No `email`, `first_name`, `phone`, `device_id` or
`account_id` appears anywhere in 1,000 live requests. Open311's GET response is clean by
design; those fields exist only in the submission.

So the rule the profile enforces hardest never fired — and the actual disclosure risk sat
somewhere a field check cannot see:

**736 of 1,000 requests carry 14 decimal places of latitude.** That is sub-nanometre
precision, published alongside a street address, on complaints like *"lawn not mowed"* and
*"backyard has not been mowed this summer, high grass, not kept up"*. Those are complaints
about the people who live at a named address, pinned to their doorstep. 999 of 1,000 carry a
street address.

**13 of 1,000 descriptions contain a phone number or an email address**, written by members
of the public into free text. One begins *"received email from Ron Author @ Street Dept"* —
naming a person in a public record.

Both were already warned about in the profile README. Neither was checked. They are now, as
**warnings** rather than errors, because neither is a schema violation and both need human
judgement:

```
52 warning(s)     against raw source fidelity
  51  household-locating coordinates
   1  description containing a phone number or email address
```

The adapter reduces coordinates to five decimal places by default — about a metre, enough to
locate an incident and not a household — which clears 51 of the 52. The remaining one is a
description, and that is correct: coordinates can be fixed mechanically, free text cannot.
Run with `--round-coordinates 0` to preserve source fidelity and see the full warning set.

## What Open311 does not give

**`agency_responsible` is free text**, present on 23 of 60 requests as a department name
rather than an identifier. There is nothing to resolve a `_core` organization from, so it maps
to `statusNote`.

**Status history is absent.** Every one of the 1,000 requests is `closed`, with a
`requested_datetime` and an `updated_datetime` and nothing between them. The `statusHistory`
the profile added after the first design review has no source here — Open311 carries current
state only, which is exactly why that gap was worth recording.

## Two response shapes

Open311 implementations disagree on the envelope. Bloomington returns a bare JSON array;
FixMyStreet-derived endpoints return `{"service_requests": [...]}` and split `title` from
`detail` where Open311 proper has one `description`. The adapter handles both.
